newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa asks union for return to negotiations.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa asks union for return to negotiations.

text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Tuesday it had demanded that union officials return to the negotiating table in its current wage dispute with workers.
A Lufthansa spokeswoman said in response to enquiries that the airline had sent a letter to the DAG white-collar workers union asking for further talks.

DAG last week said it had given Lufthansa until this Tuesday evening to come up with a better wage offer than that currently on the table, or face more of the stoppages that earlier this month grounded 35 of its flights.
The Lufthansa spokeswoman would not say if a new offer had been included in the letter. DAG said it had no comment to make on the situation at present.

DAG, which represents sections of the airline's ground and air crew, had earlier asked for a four percent increase in wages. It says Lufthansa's current offer would give its members an increase barely in line with inflation.
It is also unhappy that the airline wants the new contract to run over a period of more than two years, which DAG believes would leave workers vulnerable to future cost-cutting measures.
Lufthansa has said it is seeking to make cost improvements to allow it to compete more effectively amid the price rivalry in the airline sector.
